title: Desvigne's band: jobs and members
summary: Played dances around New Orleans during the war; lists trumpets, trombones and saxes in Desvigne's band.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years

blocks.x: Let's see. Anything else you can tell about Sidney Desby's band? Where did you work?

Well, we worked all around New Orleans with Sidney's band because we never did leave out of time with the band. We played mostly all the dances was in New Orleans at that time. It was during the war time.
I remember them too. I think they played San Jacinto club. That's right. San Jacinto, just the T-Rome. Just the T-Rome, too. Yeah. That's right. I remember that. I heard them at the San Jacinto.

We used to play two bands at the Gypsy. Yeah, at the Gypsy band. Yeah. I had a mixed band. Yeah. Yeah, I was in the neighborhood. We used to have two bands on Sunday evening. Do you remember the members of Sidney's band on the Fairroom?

Let's see now. Joe Phillips was on trumpet. Alvin Alcorn on trumpet. And Sidney's on trumpet. Eddie Pearson was on trombone. And I forgot the fellow's other name from Cross the River. He was on trombone, too. He wrote. To trombone. No, not the Rooks. Brownskin boy, collecting insurance.
Oh, yeah, yeah, yeah. We met him one time. I can't think of his name. And I told you he was a very fine trombone player.
Yeah, fine trombone player he was.
Handsome looking boy. Yeah. I remember now. Oh, he was a good trombone player. He's collecting insurance over the river. That's right, yeah. If you ever see Peter Bocai after action.
He can tell him about that. Yeah.
He played with Sidney Daphne. Yeah. Very good trombone player. He played with Walter Pichon.
Now, how old is he? He's a fairly young fellow.
Oh, yeah, he's young. He's in his studies.
That's all. Yeah. And who else?
Yeah, on the saxophone, we had Cottrell, Oscar Ruzon, Sam Lee. And in the rhythm section was William Houston and Louis Barbaran.
I'm trying to think who was playing bass with us then.
